question.text: Why does PMLA cover offences under the Prevention of Corruption Act as scheduled offences?

answer.text: Because bribery and corruption by public servants generate illicit proceeds that criminals often attempt to legitimize through money laundering
Because corruption cases are always investigated by the Enforcement Directorate exclusively
Because corruption offences are minor crimes that do not require separate prosecution
Because the Prevention of Corruption Act has been repealed and merged into PMLA

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook lists Prevention of Corruption Act offences among the scheduled offences and notes that bribery and corruption produce profits and incentives to legitimise ill-gotten gains through money laundering. Treating them as scheduled offences ensures PMLA applies to the proceeds of corruption. The Trap: Option B wrongly states that corruption cases are always investigated exclusively by the Enforcement Directorate; in practice, the scheduled-offence point is that corruption proceeds can trigger PMLA exposure, not that ED is the sole investigator. Options C and D misstate the law — corruption is not a minor offence and the Prevention of Corruption Act has not been repealed. Note: Enhanced due diligence for Politically Exposed Persons is part of the same risk picture and is reinforced by corruption being a scheduled offence under PMLA.
